title: Atomic Results Notebook — weekly rituals & micro-OKRs
content:
This is my running personal notebook for the quarter — a compact, noisy place for micro-OKRs, weekly rituals, small experiments and raw reflections. 

Intent: keep decision velocity high, track a few measurable outputs, and keep the habit of weekly closure. Not polished; expect shorthand and open questions.

STRUCTURE (how I use this)
- Top of week: quick metric snapshot + 3 focus items.
- Midweek: one-line status + blockers.
- End of week: outcome + 1 learning + next steps.
- Monthly: condense to 3 micro-OKRs and check alignment to team goals.

CURRENT QUARTER MICRO-OKRs (12 weeks) — personal slice aligned to eng-serving-runtime priorities
Objective A: Improve inference tail latency for 2-5B models in hosted API
KR A1: Reduce P95 latency for common 256-token requests from 420ms -> <=360ms (target -14%).
KR A2: Ship adaptive-batching prototype to staging and run 2 workload sweeps (baseline vs adaptive).
KR A3: Document 3 config recipes that save >=5% token-cost without observable quality degradation.

Objective B: Grow signal-on-quality tracking for my feature area (batching + KV cache)
KR B1: Build and run 8 small eval slices (e.g., prefix-heavy, staccato prompts) and capture quality delta.
KR B2: Create lightweight regression alert rule in ops dashboards and test with synthetic drift.

Objective C: 20% of work-hours dedicated to learning + mentoring
KR C1: Two 1:1 pairing sessions per month with new hires on serving-runtime basics.
KR C2: Complete the Quantization 101 short-course and do a mini writeup with 3 actionable findings.

WEEKLY RITUAL TEMPLATE (mon/thurs/sun cadence)
- Monday morning (15m): metrics snapshot, pick primary focus (the 1 thing that matters this week).
- Midweek note (10m): quick status, one blocker, next tiny step.
- Friday (20m): outcomes, what shipped, what failed, 1 learning, calendar next week.

LAST 6 WEEKS (journal-style entries)
2026-01-12 (wk1)
- Snapshot: baseline P95 420ms, infra mem pressure noted on small-burst tests.
- Focus: prototype adaptive queueing + quick perf test harness.
- Outcome: prototype queued-batcher hooked up; baseline run shows +8% throughput, but latency tail worse for spiky input.
- Learning: naive batching increases headroom but can hurt tails on bursty single-request patterns. Need prioritization heuristics.
- Next: add request-priority flag + simulate more real traffic.

2026-01-26 (wk3)
- Snapshot: P95 410ms, small improvements in stable traffic.
- Focus: add priority heuristic + lightweight KV cache warm on certain prefixes.
- Outcome: KV warm reduced some token generation stalls; throughput slightly up.
- Learning: cache warm heuristics must avoid cold-start amplification.
- Next: instrument cache-hit vs latency correlation.

2026-02-09 (wk5)
- Snapshot: ran 4 eval slices, saw small quality blips on creative prompts with cached prefixes.
- Focus: gating cache usage by prompt-type classifier (naive).
- Outcome: implemented gate; perf ok but classifier false-positive rate too high.
- Learning: small classifiers add complexity; explore heuristics before ML.
- Next: roll back to deterministic rules and expand evals.

2026-02-23 (wk7)
- Snapshot: P95 375ms on low-burst tests; staging adaptive batch turned on for 10% traffic.
- Focus: run canary and collect cost delta.
- Outcome: cost down 4% token cost for that traffic slice; one customer micro-regression flagged on long multi-turn sessions.
- Learning: preserve per-session KV affinity for multi-turn to avoid quality regressions.
- Next: quick rollback policy + per-session affinity heuristic.

QUICK METRICS (tracked weekly) — paste CSV-style small table to keep it compact
week, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens, canary_pct, eval_regressions
2026-01-12, 112, 420, $1.02, 0, 0
2026-01-19, 108, 415, $1.01, 0, 0
2026-01-26, 110, 410, $0.99, 0, 0
2026-02-02, 109, 405, $0.98, 5, 1
2026-02-09, 115, 390, $0.97, 10, 2
2026-02-23, 118, 375, $0.93, 10, 1

CURRENT BLOCKERS (open)
- Need an SRE timebox to validate canary scaling behavior (ticketed, waiting assignment).
- Shortage of labeled prompts for eval slices (ask Eval team for 200 more examples).
- Lightweight prompt classifier is noisy — consider heuristics or human rules.

EXPERIMENT LOG (quick records)
- adaptive-batcher-v1: simple time-window binning. Result: +8% throughput, tail worse on bursts. (PR #482)
- kv-warm-heuristic-1: warm when prefix matches top-100 patterns. Result: fewer stalls; cold-start amplification observed.
- per-session-affinity: preserve KV cache per session id. Result: fixed multi-turn regressions in canary.

ONE-LINER LEARNINGS (actionable)
- Always measure tail on the realistic bursty workload, not only steady-state load.
- Small ML classifiers for routing often introduce more noise than simple heuristics in early stages.
- Keep canaries small and with synthetic gating to catch regressions early.

PERSONAL HABITS TRACKER (weekly targets)
- Deep work: 9 focused hours/week on the micro-OKRs (block calendar).
- Mentoring: 2 sessions/month (30–60m).
- Learning: 3 hours/week reading or course work.
- Writeups: one short post per month (internal) summarizing experiments + 2 reproducible config recipes.

MISC NOTES / TODO (short, actionable)
- [ ] File ticket for SRE canary follow-up (JIRA-4621).
- [ ] Ping Eval team for additional labeled prompts (Slack thread: #eval-team).
- [ ] Draft mini-writeup on quantization edge cases (due 2026-03-01).
- [ ] Schedule pairing with new hire (Ida) to go over batching internals.

QUESTIONS TO ASK NEXT 1:1
- Priya: how aggressive should we be with canary % expansion for adaptive batching?
- SRE: any quick ops knobs to isolate tail increases under bursts?
- Product: acceptable tradeoffs for small multi-turn quality deltas given 4% cost improvement?

END NOTES
- This doc is an intentionally messy single-source of truth for my week-to-week decisions.
- When something stabilizes, move the recipe to team confluence and close the ticket in this doc.

Last edited: 2026-03-10 — pulled metrics, updated blockers, added per-session-affinity note.
